title: Interview with Eric Hong, VP of Engineering at Mixel, a Silvaco Company
gist: Mixel's VP of Engineering says customers' main pain is shipping complex SoCs on tight schedules with rising mask costs and IP risk, and pitches direct access to IP designers plus end-to-end support as the differentiator. He says AI-driven edge computing and ADAS are pushing Mixel into low-power interface IP and automotive/long-reach SerDes such as ASA Motion Link.

themes.theme: Customer pain: schedule, cost and IP risk

insights.claim: SoC customers must deliver increasingly sophisticated chips on aggressive schedules while managing rising development costs, IP risk and demanding power/performance/area targets, making the choice of IP partner more important.
insights.speaker: Eric Hong
insights.so_what: IP vendor quality and track record become a selection criterion as design risk rises.
insights.locator: What is the biggest challenge your customer is facing?

insights.claim: Rising mask and manufacturing costs at advanced nodes make first-pass silicon success more critical, since re-spins carry significant schedule and financial impact.
insights.speaker: Eric Hong
insights.so_what: Re-spin cost at leading nodes raises the value of silicon-proven IP and drives spend toward lower-risk vendors.
insights.locator: What challenges will your customers face in the near future?

insights.claim: Mixel claims differentiation via end-to-end support (integration, FPGA prototyping, silicon characterization, production bring-up) and by letting customers work directly with the engineers who designed the IP rather than through layered support.
insights.speaker: Eric Hong
insights.so_what: Support model is the claimed moat in a commoditising PHY IP market; unverified self-description from the vendor.
insights.locator: Why is your approach to solving this problem unique?

insights.claim: Competing approaches are broad-portfolio IP vendors with standardized support, which can slow root-cause analysis through multiple support layers, and in-house IP development, which costs engineering resources and can extend schedules.
insights.speaker: Eric Hong
insights.so_what: Frames the buy-versus-build and specialist-versus-broad vendor tradeoff in interface IP.
insights.locator: What other approaches are being used

themes.theme: AI and automotive driving Mixel's portfolio

insights.claim: AI is driving exponential growth in edge computing across consumer, automotive, industrial and IoT, raising demand for power-efficient, cost-effective connectivity.
insights.speaker: Eric Hong
insights.so_what: Edge AI growth is positioned as a tailwind for low-power interface IP vendors.
insights.locator: How has AI changed your business strategy?

insights.claim: AI-enabled systems, ADAS and connected devices are increasing the need for high-speed automotive and long-reach SerDes, and Mixel is expanding into this area including its ASA Motion Link IP.
insights.speaker: Eric Hong
insights.so_what: Automotive SerDes is a stated growth vector for Mixel and Silvaco's IP business.
insights.locator: As a result, we are expanding our IP portfolio

insights.claim: Mixel says continued gains in engineering productivity let it broaden its product offerings while helping customers cut SoC and system costs and time-to-market.
insights.speaker: Eric Hong
insights.so_what: Hints at productivity gains (possibly AI-assisted) widening IP vendor portfolios, though the source does not specify the cause.
insights.locator: Leveraging continued improvements in engineering productivity
